evidence.observation: H5 reads "when a model's redaction policy selects a verdict's roles, `message` becomes a fixed marker and `offending_facts` one marker row. A host of such a model sees which constraint failed and not the rows". At this checkout the disclosure mode decides redaction. docs/reference/disclosure.md:20 gives the default as "| unset | redacted unless `--unredacted` |". Line 210 lists `gnd verify` as "declared roles: shown under `internal`, redacted under `customer`". src/gnd/commands/verify.py:66 calls `_add_unredacted_argument(verify_parser)`. So outside `customer` mode a host of a redacting model can get the rows. docs/how-to/disclosure-mode.md already documents this, and it shows `offending_facts`, although H6 does not count that page.

§2 LR1 has the page say "what a redacting model hides (H5)", and R0.6 reads "**R0.6 One home per rule.**". Neither the LR1 steps nor the §5 citations name docs/reference/disclosure.md, `--unredacted`, `--disclosure internal` or `GND_DISCLOSURE`. The page would therefore restate a rule that already has a home, and would not tell a host how to get the rows it is allowed to see.

The plan authors "a redacting copy of" / "the reading model, and a derivation failure `(r3)`", and H2 copies "`reading_fixture/reading.orm.json` and its include `depth_fixture/vocabulary.orm.json`". The failing constraint `fact_types[subject_label].constraints[0]` is declared in vocabulary.orm.json, which reading.orm.json includes under a pinned sha256 (`25ac1974…`). src/gnd/redaction.py:97-106 reads `redact: true` from the fact type or role itself. A copy that edits only reading.orm.json therefore does not redact this verdict. The result also depends on the test process's GND_DISCLOSURE, which the plan does not pin.

concerns.recommendation: Extend H5 to cover the disclosure modes. Have the LR1 page cite docs/reference/disclosure.md and say that `--unredacted` or `--disclosure internal` shows the rows outside `customer` mode. Specify the redacting fixture as a vocabulary copy with `redact: true` on subject_label and a re-pinned include digest. Run the test with GND_DISCLOSURE unset and once under `internal`.
concerns.title: LR1's redaction case leaves out the disclosure mode that decides whether a host sees the rows
